title: Waste to Wonder Park Delhi | Timings, Ticket Price, Location & Travel Guide,
content:
Waste to Wonder Park - Delhi,

Delhi is full of surprises, and Waste to Wonder Park is one of the most creative attractions the city has to offer. Opened in 2019, this park showcases replicas of seven wonders of the world, but with a twist – they are all built using scrap metal and industrial waste. From rusted auto parts to old fans, pipes, and iron pieces, everything has been artistically reused to create stunning monuments.

This park not only entertains visitors but also spreads an important message about recycling and sustainable living. Whether you are with family, friends, or kids, a visit here is both fun and educational.

History & Highlights:

Waste to Wonder Park was developed by the South Delhi Municipal Corporation (SDMC) as an eco-friendly project. The idea was to convert scrap materials into works of art while promoting awareness about waste management.

The park features replicas of famous landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower, Taj Mahal, Colosseum, Leaning Tower of Pisa, Christ the Redeemer, Statue of Liberty, and Great Pyramid of Giza. Each structure has been carefully crafted using discarded materials, making the park a true symbol of creativity and sustainability.

Best Time to Visit:

The park can be visited throughout the year, but the best time is October to March when the weather is pleasant for walking and exploring. Evening visits are especially popular as the monuments are beautifully illuminated with colorful lights.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: The nearest metro station is Hazrat Nizamuddin (Pink Line), just 2 km away.
  • By Bus/Auto: Public buses and autos are easily available from all parts of Delhi.
  • By Car: The park is well-connected by road, and parking is available nearby.
  • The park has a dedicated parking area near the entrance, making it convenient for visitors arriving by car or two-wheeler.

Entry Ticket Price:

  • Adults (18–65 years): ₹50
  • Children (3–12 years): ₹25
  • Senior Citizens (above 65 years): Free
  • Children below 3 years: Free

Nearby Attractions:

If you are visiting Waste to Wonder Park, you can also explore nearby attractions such as:

  • Humayun’s Tomb,
  • Nizamuddin Dargah,
  • National Zoological Park,
  • India Gate,

Travel Tips: Visit in the evening to enjoy the light effects, Carry a water bottle as you’ll be walking around.Photography is allowed, so don’t forget your camera. Tickets may get crowded on weekends, so plan accordingly.
excerpt: Waste to Wonder Park in Delhi is a creative and eco-friendly attraction that showcases replicas of world-famous monuments made from scrap material. With affordable tickets, easy accessibility, and beautiful evening lights, it’s a must-visit spot for families, couples, and tourists exploring Delhi.

faqs.question: What is Waste to Wonder Park in Delhi?
faqs.answer: It’s a theme park that features replicas of the seven wonders of the world, made entirely from scrap materials and waste.

faqs.question: Where is Waste to Wonder Park located?
faqs.answer: It is located near Rajiv Gandhi Smriti Van, Sarai Kale Khan, Delhi.

faqs.question: What are the timings of Waste to Wonder Park?
faqs.answer: The park is usually open from 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM, but timings may vary on public holidays.

faqs.question: What is the entry ticket price for Waste to Wonder Park?
faqs.answer: Tickets cost around ₹50 for adults and ₹25 for children, while kids below 3 years can enter free.

faqs.question: What are the best nearby places to visit after the park?
faqs.answer: You can visit Humayun’s Tomb, India Gate, or Nizamuddin Dargah, all of which are close by.

faqs.question: Which monuments can be seen in Waste to Wonder Park?
faqs.answer: Visitors can see replicas of the Taj Mahal, Eiffel Tower, Statue of Liberty, and other world-famous landmarks.
